description: Orchestrate sandboxed coding agents in TypeScript with sandcastle.run()

latest_release.name: v0.14.1
latest_release.body:
### Patch Changes

- 2146f22: `run()` and `worktree.run()`: an aborted run no longer writes to its log file after it rejects. The agent's last buffered text is flushed, and every pending log write lands, before the run settles.
- 7430f27: `sandcastle docker build-image` and `sandcastle podman build-image` now say when the project has no Dockerfile (or Containerfile), or when the `--dockerfile`/`--containerfile` path does not exist, instead of reporting a Docker failure with "Is Docker running?". Native sandboxes don't need an image.
- 7fdca8c: Fix `claudeCode()` prompts that start with a slash command (`/code-review`, a user-invoked skill) never expanding. The print command ended in `-p -`, and Claude Code passed that `-` to the model as the first token of the prompt, so the slash command was no longer at the start. The prompt is still delivered on stdin; only the trailing `-p -` is dropped (`--print` is already passed). Thanks @andrewkcorcoran!
- 662d681: Add `"max"` to the `codex()` provider's `effort` option. It maps to `model_reasoning_effort="max"`. Thanks @joe-alphafox!
- 301c56f: Security: on git 2.54 and later, which lets hooks be defined in git config (`hook.<name>.command`), a hook defined in the repository's config could run during the git commands Sandcastle runs on the host, outside the sandbox. With a bind-mount sandbox provider (`docker()`, `podman()`, or a custom `createBindMountSandboxProvider`), a sandboxed agent could plant one when the repo uses worktree config (`extensions.worktreeConfig`, which `git sparse-checkout` sets), because `config.worktree` was writable in the sandbox. This is fixed. Sandcastle's host git now disables every config-defined hook the repository defines, including ones in files it includes under any condition, while hooks from your global and system config still run; and `.git/config.worktree` and each worktree's `config.worktree` are now mounted read-only in bind-mount sandboxes (created empty if missing), so `git config --worktree` fails inside the sandbox. Isolated providers (`vercel()`, `daytona()`) were not affected.
- 6b02c8a: `sandcastle docker build-image` in a project scaffolded for podman (it has `.sandcastle/Containerfile` and no Dockerfile) now points you at `sandcastle podman build-image`, or `--dockerfile .sandcastle/Containerfile`, instead of saying native sandboxes need no image.
- 66eb8f1: `docker()` and `podman()`: an `exec` whose engine CLI is stopped by SIGTERM before the command ends now reports a non-zero exit code, instead of 0.
- 20e5579: The `.env.example` that `sandcastle init` writes for the GitHub Issues tracker now names the extra token permissions an agent needs to push branches and open pull requests (Contents and Pull requests, both read and write). It also scaffolds `GH_HOST` (and a commented `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`) for GitHub Enterprise Server. Thanks to Adam Rackis and @Rakurai for the reports.
- daab7d3: `sandcastle init` in a pnpm, yarn or bun project now says what to add to the scaffolded Dockerfile or Containerfile when it tells you to change the install hook: `RUN corepack enable` for pnpm and yarn, `RUN npm install -g bun` for bun, before the `USER` line. The image ships only npm, so the changed hook failed every run with `pnpm: not found`.
- d42f8b2: Add `memory` and `pidsLimit` options to the `docker()` and `podman()` sandbox providers.

  `memory` maps to `--memory` (with `--memory-swap` set to the same value — a hard cap with no swap headroom); `pidsLimit` maps to `--pids-limit`. Both complement the existing `cpus` option for resource-capping untrusted workloads (e.g. fork bombs, memory exhaustion). Omitted options add no flags, preserving current behavior.

- 5cd8fd3: Fix the `parallel-planner` and `parallel-planner-with-review` templates stranding finished branches. The merge phase only took branches whose implementer made commits in the current cycle, so a branch advanced in an earlier cycle but never merged dropped out for good: its impl

detail.readme: ## What is Sandcastle? A TypeScript library for orchestrating AI coding agents in isolated sandboxes: 1. You invoke agents with a single `sandcastle.run()`. 2. Sandcastle handles sandboxing the agent with a configurable branch strategy. 3. The commits made on the branches get merged back. Sandcastle is provider-agnostic. It ships with native sandboxes that use your OS's own process sandbox (Bubblewrap on Linux and WSL2, Seatbelt on macOS), image-based providers for Docker and Podman, and cloud providers for Daytona, E2B, Fly.io Sprites, Modal and Vercel, and you can create your own. Great for parallelizing multiple AFK agents, creating review pipelines, or even just orchestrating your own agents. ## Documentation The docs live in [`docs/guide`](./docs/guide), one page per major term, with every term defined in the [Glossary](./docs/guide/glossary.md), and are published at [aihero.dev/sandcastle](https://www.aihero.dev/sandcastle). - [Getting started](./docs/guide/getting-started.md): prerequisites and a quick start - Core: [Core concepts](./docs/guide/core-concepts.md) - Sandboxes: [Sandbox providers](./docs/guide/sandbox-providers.md) - Branching: [Branch strategies](./docs/guide/branch-strategies.md) - Agents: [Agent providers](./docs/guide/agent-providers.md), [Agent sessions](./docs/guide/agent-sessions.md) - Execution: [Iterations](./docs/guide/iterations.md), [Structured output](./docs/guide/structured-output.md) - Prompts: [Prompts](./docs/guide/prompts.md) - Hooks: [Hooks](./docs/guide/hooks.md) - Init: [Init](./docs/guide/init.md) - Display: [Run logs](./docs/guide/run-logs.md) - Reference: [`run()` and `createSandbox()`](./docs/guide/run.md), [CLI commands](./docs/guide/cli.md), [Glossary](./docs/guide/glossary.md) ## Development ```bash npm install npm run build # Bundle with tsup npm test # Run tests with vitest npm run typecheck # Type-check ``` ## License MIT
